# SOP-P3-L2-03 - First-article inspection - Ring Rolling line

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, EQ-P3-L2-HT03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-017, SB-1015, SOP-P3-L2-04

1. Purpose and scope
   1.1 Purpose: Define the first-article inspection (FAI) sequence for parts processed on the Ring Rolling line for P3-L2, covering the shot blast cabinet, ring roller, and heat treat furnace to verify conformance to drawing and process requirements prior to production release.
   1.2 Scope: Applies to all first-article parts produced on EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, and EQ-P3-L2-HT03. This SOP controls inspection points, measurement methods, acceptance rationale, examples of nonconforming conditions, and records to be retained.

2. Preconditions (must be met before starting FAI)
   2.1 Engineering change notices and drawings applicable to the part must be current per ECN-2026-017.
   2.2 Equipment must be in reported-ready state in the maintenance log for EQ-P3-L2-SB01, EQ-P3-L2-RR02, and EQ-P3-L2-HT03.
   2.3 Consumables and tooling must match the part setup sheet referenced in SB-1015.
   2.4 Operator and inspector must have completed training per SOP-P3-L2-04.

3. Personal protective equipment (PPE)
   3.1 Mandatory PPE for all steps: safety glasses with side shields, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves when handling parts, and steel-toe footwear. Additional PPE for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 operations per local heat safety posting.

4. Background and rationale
   4.1 Rationale: First-article inspection validates that process settings, tooling, and equipment interactions produce a part that meets drawing tolerances and metallurgical requirements. Inspection at each process checkpoint captures defects early, reduces rework, and documents traceability to equipment and consumables.
   4.2 Example: A blast media mismatch in EQ-P3-L2-SB01 can mask machining marks, leading to false positives at final inspection. Confirming the lubricant and media per control documents prevents downstream rejection.

5. Materials and references
   5.1 Lubricant for EQ-P3-L2-SB01: CFW-LUB-463.
   5.2 Reference documents: ECN-2026-017, SB-1015, SOP-P3-L2-04.

6. Procedure — overview
   6.1 Complete preconditions and PPE checks.
   6.2 Perform process verification and in-process inspection at three control points:
       - After shot blast in EQ-P3-L2-SB01.
       - After ring rolling on EQ-P3-L2-RR02.
       - After heat treat cycle in EQ-P3-L2-HT03.
   6.3 Document results on the FAI checklist and route for sign-off.

7. Procedure — step-by-step
   7.1 Setup verification
       7.1.1 Confirm part drawing and inspection criteria called out by ECN-2026-017 are available at the workstation.
       7.1.2 Verify that the shot blast cabinet EQ-P3-L2-SB01 is loaded with the specified lubricant listed as CFW-LUB-463 and that media type matches SB-1015.
       7.1.3 Confirm tooling and chucking for EQ-P3-L2-RR02 per job setup from SOP-P3-L2-04.
       7.1.4 Record the equipment IDs and setup operator initials on the FAI checklist.

   7.2 Shot blast inspection (post EQ-P3-L2-SB01)
       7.2.1 Purpose: Ensure surface condition and cleanliness are acceptable for subsequent rolling and measurement.
       7.2.2 Inspect for media embedment, remaining scale, and uniform surface finish. Example defects: localized pitting from improper media, or residual scale obscuring features.
       7.2.3 If any nonconformance is observed, STOP the sequence and tag the part as nonconforming. Notify maintenance and reference SB-1015 for corrective actions.
       7.2.4 Record inspection results, visual observations, and corrective actions on the FAI checklist.

   7.3 Ring rolling inspection (post EQ-P3-L2-RR02)
       7.3.1 Purpose: Verify dimensional features produced by the ring roller meet drawing criteria.
       7.3.2 Measure critical diameters, radial runout, and section profiles as specified in ECN-2026-017. Use calibrated instruments and note instrument ID on the checklist.
       7.3.3 Evaluate part for physical defects such as laps, cracks, or non-uniform wall thickness. Example: a circumferential crack requires immediate containment and metallurgical evaluation.
       7.3.4 If dimensions or condition are out of tolerance, tag the part, capture measurements, and notify engineering for disposition.

   7.4 Heat treat inspection (post EQ-P3-L2-HT03)
       7.4.1 Purpose: Confirm thermal processing achieved required metallurgical properties without introducing distortion or scale beyond allowable limits.
       7.4.2 Note the process control point: quench delay maximum for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 is 13 seconds. Ensure cycle logs reflect a quench delay at or below this value; any exceeded value must be documented and escalated.
       7.4.3 Visually inspect for scale, distortion, and quench cracks. Sample hardness testing per ECN-2026-017 may be conducted where specified.
       7.4.4 Record furnace batch ID, cycle comments, and post-heat-treat observations on the FAI checklist.

8. Acceptance criteria and disposition
   8.1 Accept when all dimensional and metallurgical checks meet the drawing and ECN-2026-017 requirements and when FAI checklist is complete.
   8.2 Nonconforming parts remain quarantined and documented per SB-1015. Engineering disposition required before release.

9. Records to keep
   9.1 Complete FAI checklist for the part, including equipment IDs, operator initials, instrument IDs, and findings.
   9.2 Shot blast media and lubricant verification showing CFW-LUB-463 usage.
   9.3 EQ-P3-L2-HT03 cycle log showing quench delay values and any deviations.
   9.4 All records retained per departmental retention policy and attached to the job traveler referenced in SOP-P3-L2-04.

10. Examples and rationale for common findings
   10.1 Example: If post-blast inspection shows media embedment, the corrective action is media replacement and revalidation of the part after re-blasting. Rationale: embedded media can act as a stress riser in rolling and heat treat.
   10.2 Example: If quench delay exceeds 13 seconds on EQ-P3-L2-HT03, the part must be flagged for hardness verification and metallurgical review. Rationale: delay beyond the maximum can alter hardenability and mechanical properties.

11. Sign-off and responsibilities
   11.1 Operator: complete precondition checks and initial the FAI checklist.
   11.2 Inspector: perform dimensional and visual inspections, record instrument IDs and findings, and initial the FAI checklist.
   11.3 Process engineer: review FAI package, confirm conformity, and provide final release signature on the FAI checklist.
   11.4 All signatures and dates must be recorded on the FAI checklist before parts are released to production.

12. Revision note
   12.1 This SOP references ECN-2026-017 for drawing updates, SB-1015 for shot blast consumable control, and SOP-P3-L2-04 for operator and process training requirements.
